entry.title: Tesla S hack powered by Open Source tools
entry.summary:
The recent Tesla Model S hack is exclusively powered by Open Source hardware. Read how a Proxmark 3, Yardstick One and Raspberry Pi were used to pull of this feat.

More
entry.content:
It's been widely reported that the Tesla Model S has been successfully hacked - keyfobs can be snatched and emulated rapidly and easily.

Even more interesting is the use of 'off the shelf' hardware - a Proxmark, Yardstick one and Raspberry Pi formed the hardware backbone of the hack.
Lab401 congratulates COSIC's researchers for their hard work and responsible disclosure.
By the way - we noticed that @COSIC are using V1 Proxmarks - if you'd like to upgrade to RDV4s - send us an email!

entry.title: Proxmark 3 RDV2 Bypasses Millions of Hotel Rooms
entry.summary:
Assa Abloy's Ving Card system using the Proxmark 3 RDV2 by InfoSec firm F-Secure.

The Proxmark 3, operating in Stand-Alone mode, is able to determine the Site Master Key, and generate a master pa..

More
entry.content:
InfoSec firm F-Secure, as widely reported, have managed to cracked Assa Abloy's Ving Card system using the Proxmark 3 RDV2.

The Proxmark 3 RDV appears to:

  • Read an original hotel card in Stand-Alone mode
  • Determine the Master Key for the Site Installation
  • Use this Master Key to generate a Master Badge for the Site
  • Emulate the badge in Stand Alone Mode.

From the information and videos surfacing in the press, it would appear that F-Secure have cracked the Ving Card encryption algorithm, allowing for unfettered access to any site.

In theory, this attack could be used to:

  • Snatch a card from a hotel patron, and access any room / area
  • Upgrade your own hotel card to an all-access card

A full explanation video can be seen here:

Implementations aside, this is a testament to the Proxmark's flexibility as a device, and its Open-Source framework, easily allowing for security professionals to adapt the device to their own requirements.
